Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

reward noun and verb

also rewards, as a reward, reward someone, be rewarded, recompense, repay

classical

Quint. 1.1.20
Ter. Eun. 5.8.27: dōnum et praemium (Lewis & Short)

praemium, praemiī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a reward

The main sense of the word (Lewis & Short); also a prize (see award). To reward someone is praemiō afficere aliquem (Quint. 3.6.42) or praemium dare alicui prō rē (Cic. Mur. 8).

Other words

  • mercēs, mercēdis f. — pay, a fee; a reward

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Phaedr. 1.8.12; Cic. Div. 1.92 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    What is earned: wages, a fee, rent, and so a reward, often in a bad sense, a bribe or a penalty (Lewis & Short).

  • remūneror, remūnerārī, remūnerātus sum — to reward, to repay

    verb, first conjugation, deponent, transitive · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.44: magnō praemiō remūnerārī (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fam. 9.8.1: mūnere (Lewis & Short) · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    To pay back a kindness, with the person in the accusative and the gift in the ablative; beneficium remūnerārī, to repay a favour.

Examples

  • praemiīs etiam, quae capit illa aetās, ēvocētur

    let him be coaxed on, too, with rewards such as that age enjoysQuint. 1.1.20

  • ingrāta es, inquit, ōre quae nostrō caput incolume abstulerīs et mercēdem postulēs

    “You are ungrateful,” he said, “to have taken your head safe out of my mouth and then ask for a reward”Phaedr. 1.8.11–12

See also award, praise, punish, pay, gift.
